name: Rapture-Deep
geological_features: Kelp forests reaching from seabed to surface across entire ocean basins
Massive underwater geysers creating warm current highways
Floating mineral rafts formed by chemical precipitation
specific_features: A permanent maelstrom at the south pole three hundred kilometers across
description: Rapture-Deep is a massive oceanic world where the seas run hot and deep, heated by a hyperactive mantle that drives underwater geysers powerful enough to create planet-spanning current systems. Kelp-analogous organisms grow to prodigious heights here, their fronds forming submarine forests so dense that sunlight barely penetrates the upper canopy.

The dense, moisture-laden atmosphere sits heavy on the water's surface, creating a perpetual warm fog that parts only near the poles. The world smells of brine and growth and the sharp mineral tang of volcanic outgassing, an intoxicating mixture that early explorers compared to breathing pure vitality.

The south polar maelstrom has churned without ceasing for as long as records exist, a vortex of such scale that its roar can be detected in the planet's seismic readings. Some xenobotanists theorize that the kelp forests are a single interconnected organism that uses the maelstrom's currents for nutrient distribution, making Rapture-Deep home to the largest living thing ever catalogued.

The flora produces compounds that induce states of euphoria in most carbon-based species, a property that has made the planet both a pharmaceutical frontier and a cautionary tale. Several early research teams had to be evacuated after refusing to leave, their desire to remain on-world overriding professional obligation and even self-preservation.
